title: commercial-briefing-technical-economics-and-risk-storyline-2026
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Executive summary:

This briefing equips field sellers and solutions engineers with a concise, technical-economic narrative that explains why Redwood Inference is the pragmatic choice for customers evaluating LLM inference platforms. It bundles positioning, a short competitive brief, pricing guidance for typical purchase patterns, a compact pilot architecture, a one-page case study, and a security FAQ for prospect discovery calls. Use this document as the basis for a 15–25 minute technical sales conversation.

1) Positioning and messaging (talking points)

- Core message: Redwood reduces inference cost and operational risk while preserving developer velocity. We do this by combining a high-throughput GPU-optimized runtime, workload-aware routing, and unified operational tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Buyer pain points we address:
  - Rising token costs as usage scales (finance/engineering).
  - Inconsistent latency or cold-start variability (product/platform).
  - Audit/compliance or data-residency requirements (security/legal).
  - Fragmented tooling for deployment, monitoring, and rollouts (platform teams).
- Value levers to surface:
  - Unit economics: batching, KV/prefix caching, and model quantization can reduce tokens or GPU time by 2x–6x depending on workload.
  - Predictability: Dedicated pools and SLA-backed tiers remove throughput variance for critical endpoints.
  - Operational velocity: single API + rollout policy reduces release risk and mean time to rollback.

2) Competitive brief (2-minute summary)

- Major competitor categories: Cloud managed endpoints (cloud vendor-hosted model endpoints), LLM API providers (simple hosted APIs), and inference infrastructure vendors (self-hosted runtimes/orchestration).
- How Redwood compares (short):
  - Versus cloud vendor endpoints: better cost control via batching/quantization and unified multi-region routing; more transparent per-token cost breakdowns and rollout controls.
  - Versus LLM API providers: more deployment flexibility (Dedicated/Private), enterprise SLAs, and stronger observability for cost and latency.
  - Versus self-hosted infra vendors: less operational overhead and faster onboarding; we provide curated models and performance profiles so customers avoid costly model/stack tuning.
- Typical objection and one-liner rebuttals:
  - "We can build this ourselves." -> Rebuttal: Building a production-grade inference stack with predictable economics takes a team and months; Redwood provides a battle-tested runtime, rollout mechanics, and cost-optimizing features out-of-the-box.
  - "We need full data isolation on-prem." -> Rebuttal: Redwood Private offers a customer-controlled control plane and optional air-gapped on-prem packaging with KMS/HSM integrations.

3) Pricing guidance and quick scenarios

Summary: Redwood offers three commercial patterns: Hosted (usage-based), Dedicated (committed reserved capacity), and Private (license + support). Below are ballpark examples for field conversations — always follow up with finance for commitment quotes.

- Pricing decision factors to surface:
  - Query profile (average prompt + generation tokens, sequence length distribution)
  - Latency SLOs and concurrency requirements
  - Data-sensitivity / compliance needs
  - Expected growth trajectory (burst vs steady state)

- Example scenarios (quick reference):
  - Small startup pilot (PLG): Hosted API, pay-as-you-go. Expected monthly cost: $500–$7,000 depending on volume. Recommend enabling automatic prefix caching and a small batch size to save 20–40% on token cost during pilot.
  - Mid-market product team (predictable traffic): Dedicated monthly reserved pool. Typical commitment: $15k–$60k/month depending on GPU class and throughput; include 10% burst capacity and 99.9% uptime SLA.
  - Regulated enterprise (data residency + audit): Private deployment with license + annual support. Typical first-year TCO includes a platform license and 6–12 weeks for integration and evaluation; recommend a hybrid approach (private control plane + dedicated inference nodes).

- Pricing reference table (for internal use only, illustrative):
  | Offering  | Primary metric  | Typical starter bracket | Notes |
  | Hosted    | $/1000 tokens    | $0.80 – $5.00         | Best for trials and PLG motion |
  | Dedicated | committed GPU hrs | $15k – $60k / month   | Predictable throughput + SLA |
  | Private   | license + support | $75k+ / year         | On-prem or VPC; includes integration services |

4) Recommended pilot architecture (15–30 day technical pilot)

Objective: Validate latency, cost baseline, and observability on a representative subset of production traffic.

Steps:
  1. Discovery (3 days): collect 1–3 representative prompt templates, traffic volumes, SLOs, and integration constraints.
  2. Pilot environment (3–5 days): provision Hosted trial or Dedicated dev pool; configure the model variant, batching, and caching policy.
  3. Load & measure (7–10 days): replay anonymized traffic with 20–50% of production concurrency; capture per-request latency, GPU utilization, token counts, and error rates.
  4. Optimize (3–5 days): enable quantization profile (if acceptable), tune batch sizes, and set caching TTLs.
  5. Decision & next steps (2–3 days): present a short findings report and recommended deployment path (Hosted -> Dedicated or Private).

Pilot reference architecture (textual diagram):
  - Client service -> Redwood API (Hosted) or VPC endpoint -> Model pool (Dedicated GPUs) -> Observability (Console dashboards, traces, token-level cost)

Key pilot success metrics:
  - 95th percentile generation latency within target SLO (e.g., < 200ms for short completions).
  - Unit GPU seconds per 1k tokens reduced by at least 20% after tuning.
  - Full traceability for 100% of pilot requests; key prompts instrumented.

5) One-page case study (concise)

Company: BeaconSearch (AI-native startup)
Problem: Unpredictable inference costs and 95th percentile latency spikes affecting search relevance during spikes.
Solution: Deployed Redwood Hosted -> migrated hot endpoints to Dedicated pools, enabled KV/prefix caching and quantized model variant for production paths.
Results:
  - Cost per 1k tokens reduced by 38% (measured over 90 days).
  - 95th percentile latency improved from 620ms to 180ms for core search completions.
  - Operational overhead reduced; rollouts and canarying done via console with zero customer-facing incidents during migration.

6) Security & compliance FAQ (for prospect discovery calls)

Q: How does Redwood handle customer data in Hosted mode?
A: Tenant results and request payloads are logically isolated and stored in encrypted backends with role-based access control. We support optional request-level redaction and customer-managed KMS for keying sensitive fields.

Q: Can you run the inference runtime in our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports a VPC deployment pattern and an on-prem packaging option. The Private control plane can be customer-operated for fully air-gapped environments; integrations for HSM/KMS are supported.

Q: What audit capabilities do you provide?
A: The Console offers request-level logs, model version attribution, rollout history, and immutable audit logs for access and configuration changes. Export options to SIEMs are available (e.g., Splunk, Sumo Logic).

Q: How do you handle model provenance and third-party model licensing?
A: Models in our catalog include provenance metadata, license terms, and performance profiles. For customer-provided models we record a manifest and recommended runtime configs; legal review is recommended for commercial model redistributions.

7) Sales objection handling (quick scripts)

- "Your costs are higher than the public API." -> "We surface unit economics and provide levers (batching, caching, quantization) that reduce effective GPU time and tokens — most customers see 20–60% lower net cost after tuning."
- "We need a dedicated SLA before buying." -> "We offer Dedicated with SLA-backed latency and availability, plus a migration plan from Hosted to Dedicated to minimize friction."

8) Pitch deck outline and call-to-action

Suggested 12-slide flow for a technical buyer meeting:
  1. Title / Customer problem statement
  2. Why inference costs and reliability matter (data points)
  3. Redwood positioning and product overview
  4. How the runtime works (high level)
  5. Deployment modes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
  6. Cost control levers (batching/caching/quantization)
  7. Observability & rollback mechanics (Console screenshots)
  8. Security & compliance summary
  9. Case study (BeaconSearch)
  10. Pilot plan & success metrics
  11. Pricing patterns and next steps
  12. Ask / call to action (start pilot / technical workshop / procurement intro)

CTA options for AE/SE:
  - Offer a 30-day technical pilot on Hosted with instrumentation (preferred for PLG).
  - Offer a Dedicated proof-of-concept with a 2-week performance tuning window (preferred for mid-market).
  - Schedule a security architecture review for regulated prospects and invite Security PM.

Appendix: Operational knobs and SLO examples

- Runtime knobs list (short): batch_size, max_concurrency_per_model, prefix_cache_ttl, kv_cache_enabled, quantization_profile_id, fallback_model_policy.
- Suggested SLOs (examples):
  - Availability: 99.9% for Dedicated customer endpoints.
  - Latency: p95 < 300ms for short completions (<= 128 tokens) at steady state.
  - Error budget tracking: 99.9% success rate excluding client validation errors.

Ownership and next steps

- Primary contact (AE): list owner in CRM and tag go-to-market SE for technical follow-up.
- For security or legal questions, route to Security PM (Priya Nair) and Legal (contracts@redwood.com).
- Use the pilot checklist above and attach measurement dashboards in the follow-up email.
